disposition_reason: Tables 1-4 print regional mean ± SEM for 61 elements in 105 Greek Gruyère-type cheeses from nine regions; toxic and trace elements (including lead, cadmium, arsenic, nickel, chromium, antimony, tin, thallium, uranium, aluminium) were extracted.

study.design: Elemental profiling survey (61 elements) of Greek Gruyère-type hard cheese for authentication, safety and nutrition
study.origin: nine Greek regions (Central Greece, Crete, Epirus, Macedonia, North Aegean, Peloponnese, South Aegean, Thessaly, Thrace); sheep, goat and cow milk and mixtures
study.market: mostly small-medium dairies, the rest local markets in the respective regions
study.method: 0.5 g cheese, HNO3/H2O2 microwave digestion (CEM Mars X-Press); ICP-MS with In and Ge internal standards
lod: LOQs for all elements lower than sample levels (Table S3, not in the PDF)
study.qa: ERM-BD151 skimmed milk powder: Cd 114%, Pb 97%, Cu 115%, Fe 94%, Zn 120%, Se 142%; CRM-668 mussel tissue for REEs; recoveries 67-121% except Se

unresolved: Rare earth elements, precious metals, other ultra-trace elements (Hf, Nb, Ta, W, Zr, Th) and macro/high-abundance elements (B, Rb, Si, Sr, Ca, K, Mg, P) were not extracted as findings.

LOQs are only in Table S3 (not available).
Recoveries for As, Ni, Cr not reported in Table 9.
